learningObjectives.title: Pilgrimage, festivals and the role of the Church in the community and worldwide

questions.q: Why do many Christians value liturgical worship?
options: It provides a familiar, ordered structure that unites the congregation
It removes the need for any prayers or readings
It can only take place in a person's home
It is always completely spontaneous and unplanned
questions.explain: Liturgical worship follows a set order, giving worshippers a shared and familiar pattern of praise.

questions.q: What mainly distinguishes non-liturgical worship from liturgical worship?
options: It does not follow a fixed, set order of service
It always uses incense and set prayers
It can only be led by a bishop
It must take place at a pilgrimage site
questions.explain: Non-liturgical worship is less formal and does not follow a set structure, allowing more flexibility.

questions.q: According to the Gospels, who taught the Lord's Prayer to his followers?
questions.explain: The Lord's Prayer was given by Jesus as a model of how his followers should pray.

questions.q: Why do many Christians use set prayers such as the Lord's Prayer?
options: They give shared, familiar words that unite believers in worship
They forbid any other form of prayer
They can only be said once a year
They must be spoken silently and alone
questions.explain: Set prayers provide well-known words that allow Christians to pray together as one community.

questions.q: How is a sacrament traditionally defined?
options: An outward sign of an inward, invisible grace
A private prayer said before meals
A journey to a holy place
questions.explain: A sacrament is understood as an outward, visible sign of God's inward, invisible grace.

questions.q: How many sacraments do the Roman Catholic and Orthodox Churches recognise?
questions.explain: Catholic and Orthodox Christians recognise seven sacraments, while many Protestants recognise two.

questions.q: In believers' baptism, how is the person usually baptised?
options: By sprinkling a few drops on a baby
By making the sign of the cross in the air
questions.explain: Believers' baptism is normally carried out by fully immersing the person in water.

questions.q: Why do Baptist Christians practise believers' baptism rather than infant baptism?
options: They believe a person should be old enough to understand and choose faith
They believe babies cannot be forgiven
They reject the use of water in baptism
They think only priests can be baptised
questions.explain: Baptists hold that baptism should follow a personal, conscious decision to commit to Christ.

questions.q: Holy Communion is based on which event in the life of Jesus?
questions.explain: Holy Communion recalls the Last Supper, where Jesus shared bread and wine with his disciples.

questions.q: What is meant by transubstantiation?
options: The belief that the bread and wine become the actual body and blood of Christ
The belief that Communion is only a symbolic memorial
The belief that baptism removes all sin
The belief that the priest becomes Christ during Mass
questions.explain: Roman Catholics believe that in the Eucharist the bread and wine truly become Christ's body and blood.

questions.q: The pilgrimage site of Lourdes in France is especially associated with?
questions.explain: Lourdes is linked to visions of Mary and reports of miraculous healing, so many sick pilgrims travel there.

questions.q: The Christian pilgrimage site of Iona is located in?
questions.explain: Iona is a small island off the west coast of Scotland known for quiet reflection and community.

questions.q: Why is Easter regarded as the most important Christian festival?
options: It celebrates the resurrection of Jesus from the dead
It marks the start of the Christian year
It remembers the giving of the Ten Commandments
It celebrates the birth of John the Baptist
questions.explain: Easter marks Jesus rising from death, the central belief of the Christian faith.

questions.q: Christmas celebrates the incarnation. What does 'incarnation' mean?
options: God becoming human in the person of Jesus
The coming of the Holy Spirit
questions.explain: The incarnation is the belief that God took human form in Jesus, celebrated at Christmas.

questions.q: What do Christians remember on Good Friday?
options: The crucifixion and death of Jesus
questions.explain: Good Friday, during Holy Week, remembers the crucifixion and death of Jesus.

questions.q: CAFOD is best described as?
options: A Catholic agency working to relieve poverty overseas
A set prayer used at Mass
questions.explain: CAFOD is the Catholic Agency for Overseas Development, which tackles poverty around the world.

questions.q: A local church opens its hall each week to run a food bank for struggling families. This best illustrates?
options: The role of the Church serving its local community
questions.explain: Providing practical help such as a food bank shows the Church's role in supporting the local community.

questions.q: A group gathers, sits mostly in silence and waits for God to speak, with no set prayers or set order. This is an example of?
questions.explain: Worship without a set order or fixed prayers is a form of non-liturgical, informal worship.

questions.q: An adult chooses to be fully immersed in water to show a personal, conscious commitment to Christ. This best illustrates?
questions.explain: A conscious adult decision followed by full immersion is the practice of believers' baptism.

questions.q: A Christian travels to a shrine linked to visions of Mary and reports of miraculous healing of the sick. Which pilgrimage site are they most likely visiting?
questions.explain: Lourdes is famously associated with Marian visions and the healing of sick pilgrims.
